/images/colophon/craft-cassini_webp.title: Cassini–Huygens
/images/colophon/craft-cassini_webp.what: High-gain dish, RTG booms, and the Huygens probe — Saturn orbiter.

/images/colophon/craft-new-horizons_webp.title: New Horizons
/images/colophon/craft-new-horizons_webp.what: Compact triangular bus with a single dish — the Pluto flyby probe.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-generic_.title: Generic launcher
/images/colophon/model-launcher-generic_.what: Falcon-9-like two-stage body — the agency-keyed fallback silhouette.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-saturn-v.title: Saturn V
/images/colophon/model-launcher-saturn-v.what: Tapered three-stage stack, five F-1 bells, roll-pattern livery, and the escape tower.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-saturn-i.title: Saturn IB
/images/colophon/model-launcher-saturn-i.what: The Apollo LEO workhorse — a clustered S-IB first stage of eight H-1 engines under the same S-IVB + CSM.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-vostok-k.title: Soyuz / R-7
/images/colophon/model-launcher-vostok-k.what: Korolev-cross core with four tapered strap-on boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-5.title: Ariane 5
/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-5.what: Cryogenic core between two tall solid boosters under a bulbous fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-h-iia_we.title: H-IIA
/images/colophon/model-launcher-h-iia_we.what: Japanese cryogenic core with paired solid rocket boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-space-sh.title: Space Shuttle
/images/colophon/model-launcher-space-sh.what: External tank, twin SRBs, and the delta-wing orbiter.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-falcon-9.title: Falcon 9
/images/colophon/model-launcher-falcon-9.what: Slender two-stage body — an octaweb of nine engines, grid fins, and landing legs.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-starship.title: Starship / Super Heavy
/images/colophon/model-launcher-starship.what: Bare-stainless fully-reusable stack — 33 Raptors on Super Heavy, 6 on Starship, forward + aft flaps, and the ogive nose.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-v_.title: Atlas V
/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-v_.what: Wide RD-180 core with a bulbous payload fairing and optional solid strap-ons.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-proton-k.title: Proton-K
/images/colophon/model-launcher-proton-k.what: Soviet heavy — a central core ringed by six outboard fuel tanks.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.title: Titan II GLV
/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.what: Slender uniform two-stage that launched the crewed Gemini capsules.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-lv.title: Atlas LV-3B
/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-lv.what: Mercury-Atlas stage-and-a-half with a booster-engine skirt and escape tower.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-mercury-.title: Mercury-Redstone
/images/colophon/model-launcher-mercury-.what: America’s first crewed launcher — a slim single-engine Redstone with four tail fins, the Mercury capsule and escape tower (Freedom 7).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.title: Long March 2F
/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.what: China’s crewed launcher — core, four liquid strap-ons, and a launch-escape tower (Shenzhou).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.title: Long March 3B
/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.what: Chinese GTO workhorse — a core with four liquid strap-ons (Chang’e lunar missions).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.title: Long March 5
/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.what: China’s heavy “Fat Five” — a wide cryogenic core with four large boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-pslv_web.title: PSLV
/images/colophon/model-launcher-pslv_web.what: ISRO’s workhorse — a slender core ringed by six solid strap-on boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-lvm3_web.title: LVM3 / GSLV Mk III
/images/colophon/model-launcher-lvm3_web.what: ISRO heavy-lift — a core flanked by two large S200 solid boosters (Chandrayaan-3).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-h3_webp.title: H3
/images/colophon/model-launcher-h3_webp.what: JAXA’s new cryogenic core with solid strap-on boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-1.title: Ariane 1
/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-1.what: Europe’s first launcher — a slender three-stage 1979 design (Giotto).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.title: Long March 3A
/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.what: Core and second stage hot-staged over an open truss under a cryogenic third stage and a 3.35 m fairing, no strap-ons (Chang’e 1).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.title: Long March 7
/images/colophon/model-launcher-long-mar.what: CALT’s 3.35 m kerosene rocket for the Tianzhou freighters — a core, a second stage and four 2.25 m strap-on boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-delta-ii.title: Delta II
/images/colophon/model-launcher-delta-ii.what: Turquoise Thor-derived first stage ringed by nine white solid boosters, under a boat-tailed 2.9 m fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-ce.title: Atlas-Centaur
/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-ce.what: Steel-balloon Atlas stage-and-a-half under the white Centaur upper stage and nose fairing (Mariner 9 and 10, Pioneer 10 and 11).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-ag.title: Atlas-Agena
/images/colophon/model-launcher-atlas-ag.what: The same Atlas under a slim Agena D upper stage and a small shroud (Mariner 4).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.title: Titan II(23)G
/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.what: Two Titan core stages under a payload fairing (Clementine).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.title: Titan IIIE-Centaur
/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-ii.what: Titan core with two five-segment solid boosters, an interstage and the Centaur inside its shroud (Viking, Voyager).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-iv.title: Titan IVB-Centaur
/images/colophon/model-launcher-titan-iv.what: Titan core with two long solid motors under a 20 m fairing that encloses the Centaur (Cassini).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-falcon-h.title: Falcon Heavy
/images/colophon/model-launcher-falcon-h.what: Three Falcon 9 cores side by side — side boosters with nose cones, grid fins and legs, and a centre core carrying the upper stage and fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-athena-i.title: Athena II
/images/colophon/model-launcher-athena-i.what: All-solid stack — two Castor 120 stages, a third stage and a tapered fairing (Lunar Prospector).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-delta-iv.title: Delta IV Heavy
/images/colophon/model-launcher-delta-iv.what: Three common booster cores abreast, the centre one carrying the cryogenic upper stage and a 19 m fairing (Parker Solar Probe).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-new-glen.title: New Glenn
/images/colophon/model-launcher-new-glen.what: A single 7 m stick — a seven-engine first stage with legs and strakes under a 7 m ogive fairing (Blue Moon MK1).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-proton-m.title: Proton-M / Briz-M
/images/colophon/model-launcher-proton-m.what: Central core ringed by six outboard fuel tanks, two more stages and a Briz-M upper stage under a 4.35 m fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-sls-bloc.title: SLS Block 1
/images/colophon/model-launcher-sls-bloc.what: Orange foam core stage on four RS-25s, two white five-segment boosters, the stage adapter and upper stage under Orion and its abort tower (Artemis).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-molniya-.title: Molniya-M
/images/colophon/model-launcher-molniya-.what: Four-stage R-7 — the Blok I on its lattice, the Blok L escape stage and the probe under a cylinder-and-cone shroud (Luna 9, Luna 10).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-soyuz-fg.title: Soyuz-FG / Fregat
/images/colophon/model-launcher-soyuz-fg.what: The R-7 and its upper stage topped by the squat Fregat and the probe under a wider shroud (Mars Express).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-sputnik-.title: Sputnik 8K71PS
/images/colophon/model-launcher-sputnik-.what: The two-stage R-7 that launched Sputnik 1 — no third stage, the satellite riding under the core’s nose cone.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-soyuz-2_.title: Soyuz-2
/images/colophon/model-launcher-soyuz-2_.what: The modernised 46.3 m R-7 — four boosters round the core, an upper stage on an open truss and a long fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-antares_.title: Antares 230+
/images/colophon/model-launcher-antares_.what: Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus launcher — a 3.9 m kerosene first stage on two RD-181s under a solid second stage and fairing.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-6.title: Ariane 6
/images/colophon/model-launcher-ariane-6.what: Europe’s 5.4 m cryogenic core and Vinci upper stage under a 20 m fairing, with four solid boosters (A64).

/images/colophon/model-launcher-vulcan_w.title: Vulcan Centaur
/images/colophon/model-launcher-vulcan_w.what: ULA’s 5.4 m methane first stage on two BE-4s, the Centaur V and a 5.4 m fairing, with GEM 63XL solid boosters.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-energia_.title: Energia–Buran
/images/colophon/model-launcher-energia_.what: The 7.75 m hydrogen core with four RD-170 strap-ons and the Buran orbiter riding on its flank.

/images/colophon/model-launcher-n1_webp.title: N1
/images/colophon/model-launcher-n1_webp.what: The Soviet Moon rocket — five stages in a cone, thirty engines on the first, under the L3 shroud and escape tower.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-soyuz-7k.title: Soyuz 7K-OK
/images/colophon/model-showcase-soyuz-7k.what: The first-generation Soyuz at 7.95 m — orbital, descent and service modules, 9.8 m solar wings and the Igla rendezvous antennas.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-soyuz-ms.title: Soyuz T / TM / TMA / MS (4 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-soyuz-ms.what: The 7.48 m Soyuz across four generations — Igla antennas on the T, Kurs on the TM and TMA, Kurs-NA and a micrometeoroid shield on the MS.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-vostok_w.title: Vostok and Voskhod (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-vostok_w.what: The 2.3 m sphere on its instrument module, 4.55 m tall (Voskhod 5 m) — a belt of sixteen olive gas bottles with silver straps, hatches and portholes, antenna loops on top, and on the Voskhod the retro pack.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mercury-.title: Mercury capsule
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mercury-.what: The 3.3 m one-seat capsule on its retropack — the trapezoid window and side hatch on the cone, three retro rockets held by straps.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-gemini_w.title: Gemini
/images/colophon/model-showcase-gemini_w.what: The 5.74 m two-seat craft — the shingled black re-entry cone with its two hatches and windows over the RCS, rendezvous and recovery sections and the retro adapter.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-crew-dra.title: Crew Dragon
/images/colophon/model-showcase-crew-dra.what: The 8.1 m capsule-and-trunk stack — the white gumdrop capsule with its trapezoid hatch, four windows and SuperDraco bays over the dark PICA-X heat shield, on a trunk with a wrapped cell patch and two radiator fins, under the white hinged nose cone.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-starline.title: Starliner (CST-100)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-starline.what: Boeing’s 5.03 m capsule and service module — a broad low cone in white silver with blue stripes and the NASA roundel, over a drum with four doghouse thruster pods.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-gaganyaa.title: Gaganyaan
/images/colophon/model-showcase-gaganyaa.what: ISRO’s 5.58 m crew module and service module — a blunt white cone panelled in copper-brown tape with a trapezoid hatch and three portholes, over a drum in gold foil with two solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mengzhou.title: Mengzhou
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mengzhou.what: China’s 8.8 m crewed craft for the Moon — a grey-silver conical crew module with a red band over a white service module with gold thruster frames, two long cell wings and four engine bells.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-orion_we.title: Orion
/images/colophon/model-showcase-orion_we.what: The 7.9 m Artemis stack — the white tiled crew module over its dark heat shield, the European service module with four X-wing solar arrays, and the spacecraft adapter ring below.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-new-shep.title: New Shepard
/images/colophon/model-showcase-new-shep.what: The 19.2 m suborbital vehicle on the pad — a white booster with a black engine skirt, blue band, ring fin, three tail fins and four legs, under the crew capsule with its six large windows.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-apollo-c.title: Apollo CSM Block I / II (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-apollo-c.what: The command and service module at 10.6 and 11 m — the cone in reflective silver with five windows and (Block II) the docking probe, over the polished-aluminium service module with its white radiators, RCS quads and the engine bell.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-apollo-l.title: Apollo LM (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-apollo-l.what: The Lunar Module landed — the octagonal descent stage in crinkled gold and amber foil on four gold-wrapped legs, the faceted ascent stage with two triangular windows, RCS quads, rendezvous radar and S-band dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-shenzhou.title: Shenzhou
/images/colophon/model-showcase-shenzhou.what: China’s 9.25 m three-module craft in the Soyuz lineage — a quilted silver orbital module, the bell-shaped re-entry module on its dark ablative base and the white service module with maroon skirt, orange thruster blocks and two wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-space-sh.title: Space Shuttle orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-space-sh.what: One 37.2 m orbiter drawn once for the four sisters — Atlantis, Challenger, Discovery and Endeavour — white upper fuselage with its payload-bay doors, black-tile belly, double-delta wing with reinforced carbon edges, OMS pods and three main engines, lying on the runway.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-columbia.title: Space Shuttle Columbia
/images/colophon/model-showcase-columbia.what: The first orbiter — the only one with black chines on the wing tops, and the instrument pod on its tail fin.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-enterpri.title: Space Shuttle Enterprise
/images/colophon/model-showcase-enterpri.what: The atmospheric test orbiter — charcoal simulated tiles of foam and paint and plain white fibreglass wing edges in place of the flown tiles and carbon.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-buran_we.title: Buran
/images/colophon/model-showcase-buran_we.what: The Soviet orbiter at 36.4 m — a 24 m double-delta wing and two OMS nozzles in the tail, its main engines left on the Energia core.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-buran-ok.title: Buran OK-GLI
/images/colophon/model-showcase-buran-ok.what: The atmospheric test vehicle with Buran’s shape and mass, in painted white and grey with no tiles — its jet engines in a nacelle on each side of the fin base.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-x37b_web.title: X-37B
/images/colophon/model-showcase-x37b_web.what: The U.S. Space Force’s 8.92 m uncrewed spaceplane with its 4.55 m wingspan — black-tile underside and nose, canted tail, closed bay doors.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-progress.title: Progress 7K-TG / M / MS (3 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-progress.what: The Soyuz-derived cargo ship from 7.23 to 7.94 m — service module, refuelling section and cargo module, the 7K-TG without solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-cargo-dr.title: Cargo Dragon 2
/images/colophon/model-showcase-cargo-dr.what: The windowless uncrewed Dragon 2 on its 8.1 m trunk — cover plates where the crew version has windows and SuperDraco bays.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-cargo-dr.title: Dragon 1
/images/colophon/model-showcase-cargo-dr.what: The original 6.1 m cargo Dragon — a squat capsule 3.7 m across with four Draco quads and a white nose cone, on a 2.3 m trunk with two solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-cygnus-e.title: Cygnus Standard / Enhanced (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-cygnus-e.what: Northrop Grumman’s freighter at 5.14 and 6.39 m — a bare-aluminium cargo module in pocketed panels over a gold-and-silver service module, with flat rectangular wings on the Standard and round UltraFlex arrays on the Enhanced.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-htv_webp.title: HTV (Kounotori)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-htv_webp.what: Japan’s 9.8 m station freighter — a white propulsion module, a silver avionics section, an open pallet bay and the white pressurised carrier with dark body-mounted cells.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-htv-x_we.title: HTV-X
/images/colophon/model-showcase-htv-x_we.what: Japan’s 8 m successor freighter — a gold-blanketed pressurised module, an open cargo-support deck, a silver service module and two long narrow arrays.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-atv_webp.title: ATV
/images/colophon/model-showcase-atv_webp.what: ESA’s 10.3 m Automated Transfer Vehicle — a gold aft cone with four engines under the quilted white cargo carrier and its docking ring, with four copper-edged wings in an X.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-tianzhou.title: Tianzhou
/images/colophon/model-showcase-tianzhou.what: China’s 10.6 m cargo ship — a white propulsion drum with orange thruster blocks, a larger grey-white cargo module, the relay dish and two big wings.

/images/colophon/model-lineup-launchers_.title: Launcher line-up
/images/colophon/model-lineup-launchers_.what: Every rocket with a model, from Starship to Mercury-Redstone, stood side by side at its real height beside a 1.75 m person.

/images/colophon/model-lineup-landmarks_.title: Landmarks at true height
/images/colophon/model-lineup-landmarks_.what: Sixteen landmarks and icons hand-drawn at their sourced heights — from the Eiffel Tower and the Statue of Liberty to Michelangelo’s David, a London Routemaster and a VW Beetle.

/images/colophon/model-lineup-spacecraft.title: Capsule and spacecraft line-up
/images/colophon/model-lineup-spacecraft.what: Capsules, freighters and orbiters at true size — the orbiters lying on the runway, the capsules standing as on their rockets.

/images/colophon/model-lineup-cast_webp.title: Cartoon cast
/images/colophon/model-lineup-cast_webp.what: A flat-coloured cast at true size — man, woman, child, dog, cat, Terracotta warrior, giant panda, brown bear, giraffe and elephant — standing between the craft.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-parker-s.title: Parker Solar Probe
/images/colophon/model-showcase-parker-s.what: The 3 m Sun-grazer — a 2.3 m carbon-composite heat shield on struts over a gold-blanketed bus, with two small actively cooled solar arrays and a 0.6 m dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-solar-or.title: Solar Orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-solar-or.what: ESA’s 3.1 m Sun-watcher — a layered black heat shield with observing-port doors in front of a silver-blanketed body, six solar panels spanning 18 m, a 4.4 m instrument boom and a 1.5 m dish on the shaded rear.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-messenge.title: MESSENGER
/images/colophon/model-showcase-messenge.what: The Mercury orbiter behind its 2.5 m ceramic-cloth sunshade, on a blanketed box bus with its propellant tanks showing, two rotatable solar arrays and a 3.6 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-magellan.title: Magellan
/images/colophon/model-showcase-magellan.what: The Venus radar mapper at 6.4 m — the Star 48B motor under a ten-sided bus, a gold-blanketed equipment module and a 3.7 m high-gain dish, with two square solar panels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-akatsuki.title: Akatsuki
/images/colophon/model-showcase-akatsuki.what: JAXA’s 1.45 m gold-blanketed box Venus orbiter with a camera deck on the Venus-facing side, a flat phased-array antenna, white thruster cups and two arrays of two stacked panels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-dart_web.title: DART
/images/colophon/model-showcase-dart_web.what: The 2.6 m asteroid-impact spacecraft — two 8.5 × 2.4 m roll-out solar arrays, the NEXT-C ion engine, the DRACO camera, the LICIACube cubesat in its dispenser and a flat-plate antenna.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lucy_web.title: Lucy
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lucy_web.what: The Trojan-asteroid explorer, 16 m tip to tip — two circular solar arrays about 7 m across, a 2 m high-gain dish and an instrument platform with the terminal tracking cameras.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-psyche-s.title: Psyche
/images/colophon/model-showcase-psyche-s.what: The metal-asteroid orbiter — a 7.3 m craft with two five-panel cruciform solar arrays (25 m deployed), four Hall thrusters in a 2 × 2 cluster and 2 m instrument booms.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-europa-c.title: Europa Clipper
/images/colophon/model-showcase-europa-c.what: The 5 m Jupiter-moon orbiter — a propulsion module and radiation vault under a 3.1 m dish, 30.5 m of solar arrays carrying the REASON radar dipoles, and an 8.5 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-exp.title: Mars Express
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-exp.what: ESA’s 1.8 m box bus with gold-blanketed corners and its instruments on the nadir face, two wings of four narrow panels and a 1.6 m high-gain dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-maven_we.title: MAVEN
/images/colophon/model-showcase-maven_we.what: NASA’s 3.47 m Mars-atmosphere orbiter — a 2.3 m cubic bus, a payload platform on its boom, two gull-winged arrays with magnetometers at their tips and a 2 m dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mangalya.title: Mangalyaan
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mangalya.what: ISRO’s Mars Orbiter Mission — a 1.5 m gold-wrapped cube with its propellant-tank dome on top, a three-panel array on a boom and a 2.2 m reflector on the other side.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-hope_web.title: Hope
/images/colophon/model-showcase-hope_web.what: The UAE’s Emirates Mars Mission orbiter — a 2.9 m bus with its science deck on the front face, two wings of three panels and a 1.85 m dish on a trussed bracket.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mariner-.title: Mariner 4, 9 and 10 (3 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mariner-.what: NASA’s octagonal Mariner family — four panels with tip vanes on Mariner 4 and 9 (Mariner 9 under a foil-wrapped propulsion module); two panels, a sunshade and a 5.8 m magnetometer boom on Mariner 10.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lro_webp.title: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lro_webp.what: NASA’s 3.9 m Moon mapper — a gold-and-silver blanketed box bus with two LROC cameras, LOLA, Diviner and Mini-RF on the nadir face, a single 10.7 m² solar array on a boom and a steerable dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-skylab_w.title: Skylab
/images/colophon/model-showcase-skylab_w.what: America’s first space station as repaired — the black-skirted Orbital Workshop with its single wing and gold parasol, the airlock and docking adapter, and the Apollo Telescope Mount swung out with its four-blade windmill of panels.

/images/colophon/model-probe-sputnik-1_w.title: Sputnik 1
/images/colophon/model-probe-sputnik-1_w.what: The polished 58 cm sphere with its hemisphere seam, 36 bolts and four swept-back whip antennas of 2.4 and 2.9 m.

/images/colophon/model-probe-nova-c_webp.title: Nova-C (IM-1 Odysseus)
/images/colophon/model-probe-nova-c_webp.what: Intuitive Machines’ 4.3 m lunar lander — a 1.57 m hexagonal body, six legs, the methane engine below and three solar panels. Height and width from Wikipedia; the leg splay and deck are schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandray.title: Chandrayaan-1
/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandray.what: ISRO’s first Moon orbiter — a box bus with white radiator patches and gold-ringed instrument apertures, a 0.7 m dish on a gold boom and one solar panel on a two-bar yoke.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandray.title: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandray.what: The orbiter that carried Vikram — a bus with a gold drum rising from the top deck where the lander sat, white taped patches over its radiators and one two-panel solar wing.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-change1_.title: Chang’e 1 and 2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-change1_.what: China’s lunar orbiters — an engine bell under the bus, silver inset panels, two white relay dishes, a 0.8 m steerable dish on an arm and two three-panel wings on gold yokes.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-clementi.title: Clementine
/images/colophon/model-showcase-clementi.what: The prism-shaped lunar mapper — a sensor face with camera and lidar apertures, 12 attitude jets, a 1.07 m dish opening downward and two wings of two panels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-kaguya_w.title: Kaguya (SELENE)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-kaguya_w.what: JAXA’s 4.8 m lunar orbiter — the relay and VLBI sub-satellites on its front face, a high-gain dish on a tripod and mast and a solar paddle of three blue panels on a gold truss.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna10_w.title: Luna 10
/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna10_w.what: The Soviet 1.5 m orbiter — the braking-engine module in a white lattice skirt, cream propellant tanks and a polished pressurised instrument drum with four whip antennas and two mushroom sensors.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunar-pr.title: Lunar Prospector
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunar-pr.what: The 1.36 m drum covered in solar cells under a white nose cone, with three 2.5 m instrument booms.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-smart-1_.title: SMART-1
/images/colophon/model-showcase-smart-1_.what: ESA’s 1 m ion-drive orbiter — the PPS-1350 thruster on a gimbal arm, an instrument ring with its camera and spectrometers, a 0.3 m dish and two wings of three panels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunar-or.title: Lunar Orbiter 1–5 (5 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunar-or.what: NASA’s five camera orbiters — a bright thermal shell round the camera with its 80 mm and 610 mm lenses, four propellant tanks on truss legs, four solar panels and a 1 m dish on its boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna-9_w.title: Luna 9 (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna-9_w.what: The 58 cm landed capsule — the sealed instrument hemisphere left standing among four flopped-open petals, with the TV camera head and four rod antennas on top.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna-16_.title: Luna 16 and 24 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-luna-16_.what: The sample-return lander — a gold-wrapped hull between two torus tanks with four pressure spheres on four legs, the drill rig, and the 2 m sphere-topped ascent stage on top.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunokhod.title: Lunokhod 1 and 2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lunokhod.what: The Soviet rover — a round tub on eight wire-mesh wheels under an open dome lid, with the finned polonium-210 heat source at the back, the French corner reflector and four whip antennas.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-change-3.title: Chang’e 3 and 4 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-change-3.what: The Chinese lander — a boxy gold body on four legs with the rover ramps, tilted solar wings and a camera mast carrying the steerable dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-change-5.title: Chang’e 5 and 6 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-change-5.what: The sample-return stack — a gold octagonal ascender on the lander, with the drill tower, the folded sampling arm and the sample container beside it.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-vikram-c.title: Vikram (Chandrayaan-2 and -3, 2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-vikram-c.what: ISRO’s lander in its Chandrayaan-3 configuration — four engines and solar panels on three sides and the top, with the ramp down and the Pragyan rover part-way along it.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-slim_web.title: SLIM (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-slim_web.what: JAXA’s Moon Sniper — a 1.5 × 1.5 × 2 m prism in crumpled gold foil with a golden dome at the engine end, one strip of solar cells down a side and five round crush pads on struts.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-bereshee.title: Beresheet (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-bereshee.what: SpaceIL’s lander, 2 m across and 1.5 m high — a black deck rimmed in gold over a silver tube-frame tub with four copper tanks, four long legs and tilted blue solar plates.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-blue-moo.title: Blue Moon MK1 (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-blue-moo.what: Blue Origin’s 8.05 m lander — a hull of gold and amber foil on a pale truss base carrying the BE-7, ladder-truss legs, two tall solar-cell strips and an open octagonal cage on top.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-hakuto-r.title: HAKUTO-R Series 1 (true size, 2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-hakuto-r.what: ispace’s lander for Mission 1 and RESILIENCE, 2.3 m tall and 2.6 m across its four legs — the flown missions’ shared airframe. Height and span from ispace; the deck layout is schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-blue-gho.title: Blue Ghost (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-blue-gho.what: Firefly’s lander, 2 m tall and 3.5 m wide — a low body on four legs with its main engine below and the NASA instruments on the deck. Height and width from Firefly; the deck layout is schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-peregrin.title: Peregrine (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-peregrin.what: Astrobotic’s lander, about 1.9 m high and 2.5 m across — an open octagonal frame round two fuel and two oxidiser tanks and a helium tank, five main engines, four legs and a side solar panel. It never reached the Moon. Sizes from NASA’s NSSDCA; the frame is schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-pragyan_.title: Pragyan
/images/colophon/model-showcase-pragyan_.what: The six-wheeled ISRO rover that rolls down Vikram’s ramp.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-yutu_web.title: Yutu and Yutu-2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-yutu_web.what: The Chinese rover — a rocker-bogie on each side, a gold-wrapped warm box under a tilted solar panel, a camera mast, the arm folded under the nose and a steerable dish at the rear.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-viking-1.title: Viking landers (3 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-viking-1.what: The tripod-legged NASA lander — a six-sided deck alternately 1.09 and 0.56 m wide, gold terminal-descent pods of 18 nozzles, the sampler arm and cameras on the long forward side.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-3_w.title: Mars 2, 3 and 6 landers (3 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-3_w.what: The Soviet white sphere on four opened petals — an antenna crown of four rods, two stereo-camera ears, and the PrOP-M rover on skis tethered beside it.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-phoenix_.title: Phoenix and Mars Polar Lander (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-phoenix_.what: The solar lander on its deck — TEGA’s two ovens, MECA’s wet-chemistry cells, the robotic arm with its scoop, the stereo camera on a lattice tower and the weather mast with its lidar.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-insight_.title: InSight (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-insight_.what: The geophysics lander — the 1.8 m arm out over the ground, SEIS under its silver wind and thermal shield, and the HP3 mole deployed beside it.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-schiapar.title: Schiaparelli (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-schiapar.what: ESA’s entry demonstrator on the ground — a flat dark honeycomb crush disc ringed by a silver-gold band, three propellant tanks on struts and the DREAMS platform with its gold UHF coil.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-beagle2_.title: Beagle 2 (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-beagle2_.what: The clamshell lander opened — a gold lid dish ringed by four dark solar petals, the gold bowl base with the arm lifting out and the PAW drum of instruments.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-curiosit.title: Curiosity (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-curiosit.what: The MSL rover — six wheels on a rocker-bogie, the mast with the ChemCam head and Mastcam pair, the finned MMRTG between two white heat exchangers and the stowed arm across the front.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-spirit_w.title: Spirit and Opportunity (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-spirit_w.what: The Mars Exploration Rover — a gold warm box under a flat blue-black solar deck with four wing panels, the Pancam mast with its camera bar, a round gold dish on a stalk and six small wheels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-persever.title: Perseverance
/images/colophon/model-showcase-persever.what: Curiosity’s layout with straight-cleat wheels — the Mastcam-Z and SuperCam head, the large coring turret, the caching bay under the front and Ingenuity under the belly.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-zhurong_.title: Zhurong
/images/colophon/model-showcase-zhurong_.what: China’s rover — a wide silver deck with four butterfly solar wings, a tall mast with its camera box, two small dishes and ribbed wheels on tall legs.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-sojourne.title: Sojourner
/images/colophon/model-showcase-sojourne.what: The first Mars rover — aluminium wheels with stainless cleats on a rocker-bogie, a gold-brown warm box under a dark solar panel, the stereo camera pair and the APXS drum.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-exomars-.title: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin
/images/colophon/model-showcase-exomars-.what: ESA’s walking-chassis rover — a wheel on every leg, two wide solar wings, the gold PanCam bar on its mast and the drill box at the front.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-lrv-apol.title: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle
/images/colophon/model-showcase-lrv-apol.what: The open aluminium frame on wire-mesh wheels with titanium chevrons under tan fenders — two tube seats, the T-handle and console, the umbrella dish and the tool pallet at the back.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mro_webp.title: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mro_webp.what: NASA’s Mars mapper — two 5.35 × 2.53 m solar arrays, the 3 m high-gain dish, the 1.6 m HiRISE barrel and the 10 m SHARAD dipole. Dish, HiRISE and SHARAD sizes from NASA; the array size from Wikipedia; the bus is schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mariner-.title: Mariner 2
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mariner-.what: NASA’s 3.66 m Venus flyby — the 1.04 m hexagonal bus, two solar panels (one with its solar-pressure extension, 5.05 m across), the dish on its arm and the omni antenna atop the pyramid mast. Sizes from NASA NSSDCA; the dish and mast are schematic.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-bepicolo.title: BepiColombo (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-bepicolo.what: The stacked cruise configuration at 6.4 m — the Mercury Transfer Module with four ion thrusters and two black-and-blue wings of four panels, carrying the Mercury orbiter and Mio inside its sunshield cylinder.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-exomars-.title: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-exomars-.what: ESA–Roscosmos orbiter — the engine bell and nadir hardware, NOMAD and ACS spectrometers on the anti-Earth face, two two-panel arrays and a 2.2 m dish on a boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-ody.title: Mars Odyssey
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars-ody.what: NASA’s orbiter — folded blanket flaps on the corners, THEMIS and the cameras on the front, a 6 m lattice boom carrying the gamma-ray spectrometer, one three-panel array and a 1.3 m dish.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars2-or.title: Mars 2 and 3 orbiters (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-mars2-or.what: The Soviet M-71 bus — a banded tank barrel with its spheres, a collar carrying the black aeroshell cone and the lander capsule on top, a 2.5 m shallow dish and two big rectangular solar panels.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-phobos-2.title: Phobos 2
/images/colophon/model-showcase-phobos-2.what: The Soviet probe — four white propellant spheres round the engine, a toroidal instrument belt, a central core with equipment boxes and two horizontal solar panels on outriggers.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-tianwen-.title: Tianwen-1
/images/colophon/model-showcase-tianwen-.what: China’s Mars orbiter with the entry capsule on top — two three-panel arrays, a medium-gain dish of about 2.5 m and slender antenna rods.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-viking1-.title: Viking orbiter
/images/colophon/model-showcase-viking1-.what: The orbiter with the lander capsule under its white domed shell — an octagonal bus ring of eight bays, four solar panels on yokes, a 1.5 m gold dish and a scan platform with two cameras.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-hubble_w.title: Hubble (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-hubble_w.what: The observatory — a crinkled silver light shield with the open aperture door and the two rigid solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-jwst_web.title: JWST (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-jwst_web.what: Eighteen gold hexagonal mirror segments on their tripod over the five-layer sunshield.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandra_.title: Chandra (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-chandra_.what: The X-ray observatory — a long tapered tube with its two solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-spitzer_.title: Spitzer
/images/colophon/model-showcase-spitzer_.what: The infrared telescope — a single tilted solar panel against the cryostat tube.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-kepler_w.title: Kepler
/images/colophon/model-showcase-kepler_w.what: The planet hunter — an amber-wrapped barrel with its fixed solar panel.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-tess_web.title: TESS
/images/colophon/model-showcase-tess_web.what: The transit survey craft — four hooded cameras on a compact bus.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-gaia_web.title: Gaia (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-gaia_web.what: ESA’s astrometry observatory — a 10 m sunshield skirt round the bus.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-euclid_w.title: Euclid
/images/colophon/model-showcase-euclid_w.what: ESA’s dark-universe telescope — the baffle behind the solar-array shield.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-xmm-newt.title: XMM-Newton (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-xmm-newt.what: ESA’s X-ray telescope — a long tube ending in the mirror-module face.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-compton-.title: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory
/images/colophon/model-showcase-compton-.what: The gamma-ray observatory — a boxy instrument deck with its detectors.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-hitomi_w.title: Hitomi
/images/colophon/model-showcase-hitomi_w.what: JAXA’s X-ray satellite — the extended optical bench carrying the telescopes.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-spektr-r.title: Spektr-RG
/images/colophon/model-showcase-spektr-r.what: The Russian–German X-ray observatory — the seven-module eROSITA beside the ART-XC tube.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-voyager-.title: Voyager 1 and 2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-voyager-.what: The Grand Tour bus — a 3.7 m dish on a ten-sided body, an RTG boom of three generators end to end, the science boom with its scan platform and the 13 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-pioneer-.title: Pioneer 10 and 11 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-pioneer-.what: The spin-stabilised pair — a 2.74 m dish over the equipment compartment, two 3 m RTG booms at 120 degrees and a 6.6 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-juno_web.title: Juno (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-juno_web.what: Jupiter’s polar orbiter — the titanium radiation vault under the bus, a 2.5 m dish on top and three solar wings at 120 degrees.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-juice_we.title: JUICE (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-juice_we.what: ESA’s Jupiter icy-moons orbiter — a white tank skirt on the thrust cone, a fixed 2.5 m dish, two wings of three 3.9 × 2.2 m panels and a 10.6 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-dawn_web.title: Dawn (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-dawn_web.what: The ion-drive orbiter of Vesta and Ceres — three ion thrusters, a 1.24 m dish and two wings of five panels, 19.7 m across.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-ulysses_.title: Ulysses (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-ulysses_.what: The solar polar probe — a 1.65 m dish over the top, the finned GPHS-RTG on a stand at the side and an experiment boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-giotto_w.title: Giotto (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-giotto_w.what: The Halley flyby — a drum of dark solar-cell strips with gold bands, the Whipple dust shield on top and the tilted 1.47 m despun dish on its white cone mount.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-cassini_.title: Cassini–Huygens (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-cassini_.what: The Saturn orbiter — a gold decagon with its two main engines, the 4 m high-gain antenna, three RTGs on outriggers and the Huygens probe on its truss at the side.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-galileo_.title: Galileo (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-galileo_.what: The dual-spin Jupiter orbiter — a despun section with the scan platform, the spun drum with its louvres, the umbrella high-gain antenna, two RTG booms and a 10.9 m magnetometer boom.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-rosetta_.title: Rosetta (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-rosetta_.what: A box bus under silver-grey foil with black and gold patches, a 2.2 m dish, two five-panel solar wings of 14 m and Philae on the back wall.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-hayabusa.title: Hayabusa and Hayabusa2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-hayabusa.what: The asteroid sample-return craft — the sampler horn on its bellows, four ion engines, the return capsule and three-panel wings; Hayabusa2 adds the carry-on impactor and the MINERVA-II hoppers.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-osiris-r.title: OSIRIS-REx (true size)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-osiris-r.what: The Bennu sample-return craft — a 1.2 m dish, a 1.9 × 2.4 m solar panel each side and the 3.35 m TAGSAM arm reaching out over the front.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-venera-7.title: Venera 7 and 13 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-venera-7.what: The Soviet Venus bus — a white engine drum with rows of holes, a tank bay with its spheres showing, six struts holding the ablator-shelled descent sphere, a mesh dish on a mast and two solar wings.

/images/colophon/model-showcase-vega-1_w.title: Vega 1 and 2 (2 variants)
/images/colophon/model-showcase-vega-1_w.what: The Venus-and-Halley bus — the Venera layout with the balloon canister on the descent sphere’s crown.

/images/colophon/model-pad-apollo-lut_we.title: Launch pad: Apollo, LC-39
/images/colophon/model-pad-apollo-lut_we.what: The Saturn V pad: the 380 ft Launch Umbilical Tower with swing arms that fall away at liftoff, and the flame trench. Sizes from NASA figures on Wikipedia.

/images/colophon/model-pad-shuttle_webp.title: Launch pad: Space Shuttle, LC-39
/images/colophon/model-pad-shuttle_webp.what: The Shuttle pad: the Fixed Service Structure (350 ft with its mast), the Rotating Service Structure swung back, the 290 ft water tower. Main heights from Wikipedia; the rest approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-sls_webp.title: Launch pad: SLS, LC-39B
/images/colophon/model-pad-sls_webp.what: The Artemis pad: the Mobile Launcher tower beside the rocket (about 108 m; NASA gives 345 to 355 ft) and three lightning towers of nearly 600 ft.

/images/colophon/model-pad-soyuz_webp.title: Launch pad: Soyuz, Baikonur and Plesetsk
/images/colophon/model-pad-soyuz_webp.what: The R-7 family pad: four support arms that fall outward at liftoff, two retracted service cabins, lightning masts, the flame pit. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-proton_webp.title: Launch pad: Proton, Baikonur
/images/colophon/model-pad-proton_webp.what: The rocket alone over its flame pit: the 60 m service tower is rolled back about 340 m before launch (RussianSpaceWeb, Proton launch complex). Lightning masts approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-39a_webp.title: Launch pad: Falcon, LC-39A
/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-39a_webp.what: SpaceX at 39A: the transporter-erector that leans back 1.5 degrees before liftoff and 45 at it, the old tower extended above 350 ft. Figures from Wikipedia.

/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-cat_webp.title: Launch pad: Falcon, SLC-40 with crew tower
/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-cat_webp.what: SpaceX at SLC-40 since the crew access tower of 2023, with the transporter-erector tilting away at liftoff. The crew tower is about 300 ft (91 m; FAA).

/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-te_webp.title: Launch pad: Falcon, SLC-40 and SLC-4E
/images/colophon/model-pad-f9-te_webp.what: A bare Falcon pad: the transporter-erector tilting away at liftoff, and lightning masts. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-starbase_webp.title: Launch pad: Starship, Starbase
/images/colophon/model-pad-starbase_webp.what: The Starbase launch tower with its catching arms held open. Tower height approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-atlas-v_webp.title: Launch pad: Atlas V, SLC-41
/images/colophon/model-pad-atlas-v_webp.what: The ULA pad: mobile launch platform, umbilical tower and four lightning towers; the Vertical Integration Facility stands off the pad and is left out. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-cape-classic_.title: Launch pad: Cape service-tower pad
/images/colophon/model-pad-cape-classic_.what: The Cape's Atlas, Delta, Titan and Saturn IB pads: an umbilical tower with swing arms beside the vehicle. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-kourou-a5_web.title: Launch pad: Ariane 4 and 5, Kourou
/images/colophon/model-pad-kourou-a5_web.what: The ELA-2 and ELA-3 pads: an umbilical mast beside the launcher and four tall lightning towers. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-kourou-a6_web.title: Launch pad: Ariane 6, Kourou
/images/colophon/model-pad-kourou-a6_web.what: The ELA-4 pad: the umbilical mast, two lightning towers and the mobile gantry rolled well back. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-chinese-fst_w.title: Launch pad: Chinese service tower
/images/colophon/model-pad-chinese-fst_w.what: The fixed service tower of Jiuquan, Xichang, Wenchang and Taiyuan, its working platforms folding away at liftoff. Jiuquan's crewed-launch tower is 89.5 m plus a 16 m lightning rod (CMSE) and is drawn for every Jiuquan launch; the others are approximate.

/images/colophon/model-pad-tanegashima_w.title: Launch pad: Tanegashima
/images/colophon/model-pad-tanegashima_w.what: The Yoshinobu pad: the H-II mobile launcher, 65.5 m high, and a 74.5 m lightning tower (JAXA).

/images/colophon/model-pad-sriharikota_w.title: Launch pad: Sriharikota
/images/colophon/model-pad-sriharikota_w.what: The ISRO pad: the umbilical tower beside the vehicle and the mobile service tower rolled well back. Sizes approximate.

/images/colophon/model-moon-apollo-lm_we.title: Apollo Lunar Module
/images/colophon/model-moon-apollo-lm_we.what: Descent + ascent stage, gold MLI foil, and RCS quads.

/images/colophon/model-moon-apollo-lm-ex.title: Apollo LM (J-mission + LRV)
/images/colophon/model-moon-apollo-lm-ex.what: Extended-stay LM paired with the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

/images/colophon/model-moon-luna-9_webp.title: Luna 9
/images/colophon/model-moon-luna-9_webp.what: Soviet sphere that returned the first images from the lunar surface.

/images/colophon/model-moon-luna-sample-.title: Luna sample-return
/images/colophon/model-moon-luna-sample-.what: Ascent rocket atop a descent platform (Luna 16 / 20 / 24).

/images/colophon/model-moon-lunokhod_web.title: Lunokhod rover
/images/colophon/model-moon-lunokhod_web.what: Eight-wheeled Soviet rover with a clamshell solar lid.

/images/colophon/model-moon-chang-e-land.title: Chang’e lander
/images/colophon/model-moon-chang-e-land.what: CNSA descent stage with ascent capsule (Chang’e 5 / 6).

/images/colophon/model-moon-yutu_webp.title: Yutu rover
/images/colophon/model-moon-yutu_webp.what: Six-wheeled Chinese rover with folding solar panels.

/images/colophon/model-moon-chandrayaan-.title: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram
/images/colophon/model-moon-chandrayaan-.what: ISRO four-leg lander that delivered the Pragyan rover.

/images/colophon/model-moon-slim_webp.title: SLIM
/images/colophon/model-moon-slim_webp.what: JAXA precision “Moon Sniper” two-engine descent stage.

/images/colophon/model-mars-viking_webp.title: Viking
/images/colophon/model-mars-viking_webp.what: Tripod-legged NASA lander with RTG and sampling arm.
